annotations.title: Look up a job: AI, outlook, fit and routes in

description: Looks up one named job or profession and returns everything OffLadder has written about it, for someone worried about their own job or weighing one to move into, e.g. 'will AI replace accountants', 'is my job as a paralegal safe from AI', 'will AI take software engineering jobs', 'is graphic design a dying career', 'what is the outlook for veterinarians', 'is nursing right for me', 'is cybersecurity a good career', 'how do I become an electrician', 'how to become a nurse practitioner', 'what can teachers do instead of teaching', 'careers after leaving law'. Covers 228 jobs across health, tech and data, finance, creative work, the trades, science, education and public service. For each job it returns the guides that exist: whether the work suits you and how to try it, how people get in, where the job is heading, what AI changes in it (which tasks are being automated and which stay with people), and what people move on to. Each guide comes with its direct answer, key points and primary sources such as the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, the International Labour Organization and the World Economic Forum. Says plainly when OffLadder has not written about a job. Does not list open vacancies or what a named employer pays, and never gives a percentage chance of replacement or a made-up forecast.

about.description: What they want to know: 'ai' (what AI changes in the job), 'future' (where the job is heading), 'fit' (whether it would suit them), 'route' (how to get in) or 'leaving' (what to do after it). Left out, every guide on the job comes back.

job.description: The job, profession or field, in the person's words, e.g. 'accountant' or 'graphic design'.
